content:
content warning: oops! all throatclearing :(

by the way, there are some blatant textual parallels between how to get a friend to leave an abusive relationship and on friends at frontier labs. a lot of my recent writing (on antimemes, and easier to be good) have been building up scaffolding and getting some loud tangents out of the way, so that i can write on friends at frontier labs and clarify my own thinking on the matter. all of those other pieces contain models that seem strongly but only partially instructive when i think about having friends at labs.

after several false starts in writing on friends at frontier labs, what got the words to flow was to put the draft side by side with my finished piece on abusive relationships, and to let myself self-plagiarize generously.

this unfortunately sort of leaves a shadowy rhetorical move where i am strongly implying that frontier labs are like abusive romantic partners, but i do not endorse this in any real way.

like, often things are like other things, but it's not that deep! for example, some similarities are:

  • people tend to spend time focusing on what is important to them
  • it is easier to get mad at people and yell at them when you want to get them to stop doing a thing, but it seems to me like often the more productive thing to do is to provide them lots of support, so that they have a little more slack
  • it's can be helpful to model people as being conflicted and confused under stressful environments, and then think "what kinds of support would I appreciate when I am conflicted and confused under stressful environments".

to put it another way, maybe there's like, what, a 30% similarity between these two things, but other things that can share a 30% similarity to an abusive relationship include

  • having a newborn
  • founding a startup
  • training for the olympics
  • caring for a parent with dementia
  • entirely healthy romantic relationships

such that i do not really endorse any amount of valence rub-off.

the obvious difference that the lab employees are not being negatively coerced to stay. the frontier labs are not holding any lab employees hostage, and the reason that they are staying is because they seem to truly believe that they are doing the right thing.

i think the strongest opinion i really have at this point is like, hey if you are trying to get lab employees to quit by getting mad at them (which i think is a framing that the deeprats don't endorse, but somehow this is the felt experience of everyone i know who is working at a lab) this seems counterproductive to your own goals.

i am aware that that take makes me "atheist telling the christians that they are practicing their religion wrong"-coded, but you know what sometimes that is what being a blogger is all about.
